rv.q: O’Donnell efficiently and effectively ties up the family tales of her life by ultimately circling back to her own mother.
Rosie O’Donnell uses her muscles grown in years of standup to craft a solid and tender solo show about grief, parenthood, and finding home where your children are.
It’s already a moving show, and it’s only going to get better for her from here.

cn.t: O'Donnell returns to the stage with panache in this autobiographical solo show that blends comedy with personal storytelling about motherhood, identity, and recent life changes, though it largely sidesteps her Hollywood career and famous feuds.
